items.english: Another is a monk of strikingly antique aspect, in a yellow robe with a small bronze ring hung from his ear. His skin is remarkably black in colour, and to judge from his curled hair and beard, he would seem to be a man come from somewhere west of the Congling Mountains. Until now he has been patiently flourishing a red-handled shubi to drive off the horseflies and flies that would settle upon the naked man, but he appears at last to have tired a little, and now he has come over beside the unglazed earthen jar and squats there portentously, in the attitude of a turkey.
notes: Congling: the Onion Ranges, the Pamirs; the text's vague learned geography for a westerner, kept as a name. shubi: a horsehair fly-whisk with religious and scholar-official use; kept here on first use and then as fly-whisk, as the fan and jar are planted as unexplained objects.

items.english: The last stands far apart from these two, under the eaves of a thatched hut in the corner of the threshing-floor. This man grows only a perfunctory beard like a rat's tail on the tip of his chin, and wears a black cloth gown long enough to hide his heels, with a tea-brown sash whose knot hangs sloppily. To judge from the manner in which from time to time he preciously plies a fan made of white birds' feathers, he is most likely a Confucian scholar or something of the kind.
notes: Third man left as conjecture, as in the Japanese; his name, Sun Sensei, and the fan's ownership are not given until Part II, so not anticipated here.

items.english: All three, as if by agreement, keep their mouths shut. What is more, they hardly so much as move, as though they took extraordinary interest in something now about to happen, and for that reason were all holding their breath.

data.say: Drafted the held tableau p4-p6 in present-tense deadpan, keeping jar, fan, and silence unidentified.
